2026-10-22 batch settlement extraction: ResultSettlementCoordinator still calls the injected DeliveryCustodyFacade once per real member; it submits AcknowledgeMessageCommand to the Inbox owner. Timeout retains the Harness result claim. This is a typed facade call, not direct InboxService mutation; composition and mutation-thread controls pin the boundary.

2026-09-28 actor composition: the dispatch cadence effect dismisses an accepted offer notice via DeliveryCustodyFacade and DismissSystemNoticeCommand. The Inbox owner remains the writer and shutdown drains offers before Inbox closure; this records the new actor-mode call site alongside the retained offline path.

2026-09-28 actor composition: this is bound-method capture for HoldRefreshCoordinator, not execution during start. Its bounded effect calls DeliveryCustodyFacade, submitting RefreshHoldCommand to the Inbox owner; native RX and maintenance do not perform the mutation.

2026-09-28 actor composition: this is bound-method capture for ProgressPublishCoordinator. Its bounded effect calls DeliveryCustodyFacade and SubmitProgressCommand; local writes remain on Inbox owner and remote progress goes through DeliveryIoWorker. No raw service/native call is introduced here.

WP5-A (ruling 61): the headless turn end stamps the first fetched time and clears non-terminal failure retries for one already-injected row through DeliveryCustodyFacade's FetchPendingCommand(message_id, completed_turn=True). It is a typed facade call, not a raw InboxService mutation.

WP5-A rework (ruling 74): the one-shot startup sweep acks a stamped pending row only when settle_hint_for says ack. It is a typed DeliveryCustodyFacade ack, the same call the claimed-result settlement makes.

2026-09-21: the fail-loud notice to the original sender is a first-class inbox submission through the composed port (the same seam the mechanism answer functions use). It is not a raw service bypass; the notice is idempotent per attempt and never settles the original delivery.

2026-10-15 #1465 (#1463 finding 2) fail-loud alarm seam, same class as DaemonEventBridge._submit_loud: last-resort human alarm when a failed delivery has no pending row, no settlement tombstone and no ledger route. It reads the inbox's composed alarm_emitter port and emits through the existing throttle ledger; it never submits, acks or settles a delivery and introduces no raw service/native call, which is why it is a legitimate manifested raw bypass.

2026-10-14 WP7: the reply reminder writes its durable system notice through the injected inbox port. In composition that port is the DeliveryCustodyFacade, whose receive_system_notice sends ReceiveSystemNoticeCommand to the Inbox owner; this adapter never constructs or mutates a raw InboxService.

WP5-A accepted-only stamp: after a worker accepts a batch offer, the runtime asks the composed DeliveryCustodyFacade to stamp the accepted members via FetchPendingCommand. This is a typed facade call, not a raw InboxService mutation; it is idempotent, bounded to the accepted member set, and retried through the pending-fetch map without opening a second settlement path.

WP5-A retry of the accepted-only stamp: a failed facade fetch is retried from the bounded in-memory pending map on the next tick. The composed DeliveryCustodyFacade submits FetchPendingCommand to the Inbox owner; this is not a raw service write and cannot revive a settled batch.
